prompt:
Write 10 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a low-speed head-on collision claim, in time order. Injury: wrist fracture. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1368; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- It is not yet clear whether the injury came from this crash.
- Treatment ran somewhat longer than usual for this injury.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver lives with the policyholder and is covered as a household member.
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened after a low-speed head-on collision reported by the claimant, who was driving the insured vehicle at the time. The claimant reports a wrist injury and states they are not represented by an attorney.

Entry 2: Reviewed the police report, which confirms the claimant was in the vehicle at the scene. Scheduled a call to take a full statement and request the claimant's medical records.

Entry 3: Claimant gave a statement today and described the impact the same way as on first notice of loss. No new details have emerged, and the account has stayed consistent across every conversation so far.

Entry 4: Photos from the scene and the repair estimate show damage that lines up with the described impact. No independent witnesses have come forward, so the photos are the main evidence of how the collision happened.

Entry 5: Confirmed with the policyholder that the claimant lives in the household and is a listed driver under the policy, so coverage applies to the claimant as a household member. Checked the policy effective history and found nothing indicating the vehicle damage predates the coverage start.

Entry 6: Requested prior vehicle records and inspected the repair file. No earlier damage to the vehicle is on record, and nothing in the file suggests a prior loss.

Entry 7: Medical records received show a wrist fracture treated with a longer course of care than is typical for this injury. Requested additional treatment notes to understand the timeline of care.

Entry 8: Searched available records and asked the claimant about prior problems. No earlier injury to the same area of the body is known, but the claimant's prior history is still being confirmed with the provider.

Entry 9: The medical file does not yet establish whether the fracture was caused by this collision. Referred the file to the medical review team for an opinion on causation and the link between the crash and the injury.

Entry 10: Status remains open pending the medical review and the remaining treatment records. Will follow up with the claimant once the causation opinion is back to discuss next steps.
